paragraphs: Limoneira Company, a Delaware corporation, is the successor to several businesses with operations in California since 1893. Our business and operations are described below. For detailed financial information with respect to our business and our operations, see our consolidated financial statements and the related notes to consolidated financial statements, which are included in Item 8 in this Annual Report. In addition, general information concerning our Company can be found on our website at www.limoneira.com. All of our filings with the SEC, including but not limited to, Annual Reports on Form 10-K, Quarterly Reports on Form 10-Q, Current Reports on Form 8-K, and any amendments thereto, are available free of charge on our website as soon as reasonably practicable after such material is electronically filed with or furnished to the SEC. The contents of our website referred to above are not incorporated into this Annual Report. Further, any references to our website are intended to be interactive textual references only.

We are primarily an agribusiness company founded and based in Santa Paula, California, committed to responsibly using and managing our approximately 10,500 acres of land, water resources and other assets to maximize long-term stockholder value. Our operations consist of fruit production, sales and marketing, rental operations, real estate and capital investment activities.
Agribusiness activities are performed through these four reporting segments:

We are one of California's oldest citrus growers and according to the California Avocado Commission, we are one of the largest growers of avocados in the United States. In addition to growing lemons and avocados, we grow oranges and wine grapes. We have agricultural plantings throughout Ventura and San Luis Obispo Counties in California, Yuma County in Arizona, La Serena, Chile and Jujuy, Argentina, which collectively consist of approximately 3,100 acres of lemons, 1,500 acres of avocados, 100 acres of oranges and 400 acres of wine grapes. We also operate our own packinghouses in Santa Paula, California and Yuma, Arizona, where we process, pack and sell lemons that we grow, as well as lemons grown by others. We have a 47% interest in Rosales S.A. ("Rosales"), a citrus packing, marketing and sales business, a 90% interest in Fruticola Pan de Azucar S.A. ("PDA"), a lemon and orange orchard and a 100% interest in Agricola San Pablo, SpA ("San Pablo"), a lemon and orange orchard, all of which are located near La Serena, Chile. We have a 51% interest in a joint venture, Trapani Fresh Consorcio de Cooperacion ("Trapani Fresh"), a lemon orchard in Argentina.

Our water resources include water rights, usage rights and pumping rights to the water in aquifers under, and canals that run through, the land we own. Water for our farming operations is sourced from the existing water resources associated with our land, which includes rights to water in the adjudicated Santa Paula Basin (aquifer) and the un-adjudicated Fillmore and Paso Robles Basins (aquifers). We also use surface water in Arizona from the Colorado River through the Yuma Mesa Irrigation and Drainage District ("YMIDD"). We use ground water provided by wells and surface water for our PDA and San Pablo farming operations in Chile and our Trapani Fresh farming operations in Argentina.

For more than 100 years, we have been making strategic investments in California agriculture and real estate. We currently have an interest in two real estate development projects in California. These projects include multi-family housing, single-family homes and apartments of approximately 800 units in various stages of planning and development.

In January 2025, we completed three separate sale transactions of Santa Paula Basin water pumping rights at a selling price of $30,000 per acre-foot, totaling $1.7 million and recorded a gain on sales of water rights of $1.5 million.

On March 1, 2025, we received a notice of termination from PGIM Real Estate Finance, LLC ("PGIM") regarding The Farm Management Agreement ("FMA") dated January 31, 2023. The FMA was terminated effective March 31, 2025. Under the FMA, we provided farming, management and operations related to the 3,537 acres in Tulare County, California (the "Northern Properties"), which we previously sold to PGIM.

On March 17, 2025, we announced that our Board of Directors approved a share repurchase program authorizing us to repurchase up to $30.0 million in shares of our outstanding common stock. The share repurchase program may be modified, suspended or discontinued at any time and does not commit us to repurchase any shares.

On March 17, 2025, we announced that we formally concluded our process to explore potential strategic alternatives that we previously announced on December 1, 2023. While this formal exploration process has concluded, we remain committed to executing our comprehensive strategic roadmap to create long-term stockholder value. As part of our normal course of business, we will continue to be opportunistic in evaluating potential strategic merger and acquisition opportunities, while also advancing our initiatives to monetize non-core assets.

On April 8, 2025, we announced that we are entering into a letter of intent to form a 50%/50% joint venture with Agromin Corporation, the largest organics waste recycler in California, to significantly expand Agromin Corporation's successful organic waste recycling program. The joint venture plans to expand from the existing 15-acre green waste composting facility at Limoneira Ranch in Santa Paula into a 70-acre, commercial-scale composting facility capable of processing green waste and food waste. We expect to enter into the joint venture and begin construction in fiscal year 2026.

On April 9, 2025, we announced that we received a cash distribution of $10.0 million representing our share of a $20.0 million cash distribution from our real estate joint venture, Harvest at Limoneira, with the Lewis Group of Companies ("Lewis").

On June 6, 2025, we entered into a Commercial Packinghouse License Agreement with Sunkist Growers, Inc., a nonprofit marketing cooperative ("Sunkist"), effective as of November 1, 2025. The agreement permits us to grade, label, pack, prepare for marketing by Sunkist and ship Sunkist grower fruit, and to use Sunkist trademarks in these activities. The agreement has an initial term of three years with automatic one-year extensions. In relation to our decision to merge our sales and marketing operations into Sunkist, we incurred cash and stock compensation severance expenses of approximately $0.7 million in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025.

On June 26, 2025, we entered into a Master Loan Agreement (the "MLA") with AgWest Farm Credit, PCA (the "Lender"), dated June 26, 2025, together with a revolving credit facility supplement (the "Revolving Credit Supplement") and a non-revolving credit facility supplement (the "Non-Revolving Credit Supplement" and together with the Revolving Credit Supplement, the "Supplements"). The MLA amends and restates the previous Master Loan Agreement between us and the Lender and extends the principal repayment to July 1, 2030.

headings: Risks Related to Our Agribusiness Operations
Our decision to merge our citrus sales and marketing operations into Sunkist Growers, Inc. beginning November 1, 2025 may not be successful.

Adverse weather conditions, natural disasters, including earthquakes and wildfires, and other natural conditions, including the effects of climate change, could impose significant costs and losses on our business.

Our agricultural plantings are potentially subject to damage from disease and pests, which could impose losses on our business and the prevention of which could impose significant additional costs on us.
Our earnings are sensitive to fluctuations in market supply and prices and demand for our products.
Our earnings may be subject to seasonal variability.
Increases in commodity or raw product costs, such as fuel and paper, could adversely affect our operating results.
Increases in labor, personnel and benefits costs could adversely affect our operating results.
Changes in immigration laws could impact the ability of Limoneira to harvest its crops.
The lack of sufficient water would severely impact our ability to produce crops or develop real estate.
The use of herbicides, pesticides and other potentially hazardous substances in our operations may lead to environmental damage and result in increased costs to us.
A global economic downturn may have an adverse impact on participants in our industry, which cannot be fully predicted.
We are subject to the risk of product contamination and product liability claims.
We are subject to transportation risks.
Events or rumors relating to LIMONEIRA or our other trademarks and related brands or Sunkist could significantly impact our business.
Government regulation could increase our production costs and increase legal and regulatory expenses.
We depend on our infrastructure to have sufficient capacity to handle our annual lemon production needs.
Risks Related to Our Indebtedness
We may be unable to generate sufficient cash flow to service our debt obligations.
Some of our debt is based on variable rates of interest, which could result in higher interest expenses in the event of an increase in the interest rates.
Global capital and credit market issues affect our liquidity, increase our borrowing costs and may affect the operations of our suppliers and customers.
Risks Related to Our Real Estate Development Operations
We are involved in a cyclical industry and are affected by changes in general and local economic conditions.
A recession in the global economy, or a downturn in national or regional economic conditions, could adversely impact our real estate development business.
Higher interest rates and lack of available financing can have significant impacts on the real estate industry.
We are subject to various land use regulations and require governmental approvals for our developments that could be denied.
Third-party litigation could increase the time and cost of our real estate development efforts.

We are subject to environmental regulations and opposition from environmental groups that could cause delays and increase the costs of our real estate development efforts or preclude such development entirely.
Our real estate development projects are concentrated entirely in California.
If the real estate industry weakens or instability of the mortgage industry and commercial real estate financing exists, it could have an adverse effect on our real estate activities.
We rely on contractual arrangements with third-party advisors to assist us in carrying out our real estate development projects and are subject to risks associated with such arrangements.
If we are unable to complete land development projects within forecasted time and budget expectations, if at all, our financial results may be negatively affected.
If we are unable to obtain required land use entitlements at reasonable costs, or at all, our operating results would be adversely affected.

We could experience a reduction in net income or reduced cash flows if we are unable to obtain reasonably priced financing to support our real estate development projects and land development activities.
We may encounter risks associated with the real estate joint ventures we have with the Lewis Group of Companies, including:
We may encounter other risks that could impact our ability to develop our land.
General Risks and Risks Related to Our Common Stock
Our business is highly competitive, and we cannot assure you that we will maintain our current market share.
Currency exchange fluctuation may impact the results of our operations.
We are dependent on key personnel and the loss of one or more of those key personnel may materially and adversely affect our prospects.
Inflation can have a significant adverse effect on our operations.
The acquisition of other businesses could pose risks to our operating income.
The value of our common stock could be volatile.
Concentrated ownership of our common stock creates a risk of sudden change in our share price.
Our charter documents contain provisions that may delay, defer or prevent a change of control.
We incur increased costs as a result of being a publicly traded company.
paragraphs: The merging of our citrus sales and marketing operations into Sunkist reduces our ability to exercise control over the sales and marketing of our lemons. Sunkist marketing may be ineffective, which could result in decreased sales of citrus and, in particular, the sales of our lemons. Insufficient resources committed by Sunkist to the sales and marketing of citrus may reduce the sales of our lemons and adversely affect our operations and financial results.

Consumer and institutional recognition of Sunkist trademarks and related brands and the association of these brands with high quality and safe citrus is an integral part of the Sunkist business. The occurrence of any events or rumors that cause consumers and/or institutions to no longer associate those brands with high quality and safe citrus may materially affect the value of their brand names and the demand for fresh citrus.

As a Sunkist-licensed packinghouse, we are required to purchase the majority of our packing supplies from Fruit Growers Supply Company ("FGS"), a manufacturing and supply cooperative affiliated with Sunkist. Increased costs for packing supplies from FGS or an extended interruption in the shipping of packing supplies could negatively affect our operating income.

Sunkist cybersecurity risks, data protection breaches, cyber-attacks and system integration issues could disrupt Sunkist internal operations or services provided to end customers, and such disruption could reduce our expected revenue, increase our expenses, damage our reputation and adversely affect our business.

Fresh produce is vulnerable to adverse weather conditions, including windstorms, floods, drought and temperature extremes, which are quite common and may occur with higher frequency or be less predictable in the future due to the effects of climate change. Unfavorable growing conditions can reduce both crop size and crop quality. In extreme cases, entire harvests may be lost in some geographic areas. We purchase crop insurance for certain crops which partially mitigates our exposure.

All of our crops are subject to damage from frosts and freezes, and this has happened periodically in the past. In some cases, the fruit is damaged or ruined; in the case of extended periods of cold, the trees can also be damaged or killed.

paragraphs: Limoneira Company, 一間 Delaware 公司, 是自 1893 年以來在加州運作的數家企業的繼承者。我們的業務與運作於下文說明。有關我們業務與運作的詳細財務資訊，請參閱我們的合併財務報表及相關合併財務報表附註，這些內容包含於本年度報告的第 8 項。此外，有關本公司的一般資訊，可於我們的網站 www.limoneira.com 查閱。我們向 SEC 提交的所有申報文件，包括但不限於年度報告表 10-K、季報表 10-Q、現況報告表 8-K 及任何修正案，均會在這些資訊電子提交或提供給 SEC 後儘速於我們的網站上免費提供。上文提及的網站內容並未納入本年度報告。此外，任何提及我們網站的參考，僅為互動文字參考。
我們主要為一家農業企業，創立並設立於加州聖塔安那，致力於 responsibly 使用與管理我們約 10,500 英畝的土地、水資源及其他資產，以最大化長期股東價值。我們的運作包括水果生產、銷售與行銷、租賃業務、不動產及資本投資活動。
農業業務活動透過以下四個應報告分部進行：

我們是加州最古老的柑橘種植者之一，根據加州牛油果委員會的資料，我們是美國最大的牛油果種植者之一。除了種植檸檬與牛油果，我們也種植橙子與葡萄酒釀造用葡萄。我們在加州的文圖拉縣與聖路易斯奧比縣、亞利桑那州的尤馬縣、智利的拉塞爾納與阿根廷的胡胡伊縣均有農業種植，這些種植地總計約有 3,100 英畝的檸檬、1,500 英畝的牛油果、100 英畝的橙子與 400 英畝的葡萄酒釀造用葡萄。我們也在加州聖塔安那與亞利桑那州尤馬設有自有包裝廠，處理、包裝與銷售我們種植的檸檬，以及他人種植的檸檬。我們在智利拉塞爾納附近擁有 Rosales S.A. ("Rosales") 的 47% 股權，這是一家柑橘包裝、行銷與銷售業務；擁有 Fruticola Pan de Azucar S.A. ("PDA") 的 90% 股權，這是一家檸檬與橙子種植園；以及擁有 Agricola San Pablo, SpA ("San Pablo") 的 100% 股權，這是一家檸檬與橙子種植園。我們在阿根廷的拉普拉塔新鮮合作社 ("Trapani Fresh") 聯合企業中擁有 51% 股權，這是一家檸檬種植園。

我們的水資源包括水權、使用權與抽水權，用以抽取我們所有土地下的含水層與穿過土地的水道中的水。我們農業運作所使用的水來自與我們土地相關的現有水資源，包括聖塔安那盆地（含水層）的 adjudicated 水權，以及未 adjudicated 的 Fillmore 和 Paso Robles 盆地（含水層）的水權。我們也在亞利桑那州透過 Yuma Mesa 灌溉與排水區（"YMIDD"）使用科羅拉多河的地表水。我們在智利的 PDA 與 San Pablo 農業運作以及阿根廷的 Trapani Fresh 農業運作中，使用地下水與地表水。
在超過 100 年的時間裡，我們持續在加州農業與不動產上進行戰略投資。我們目前在加州擁有兩個不動產開發項目。這些項目包括多戶住宅、單戶住宅與公寓，總計約有 800 個單位，處於不同階段的規劃與開發中。
2025 年 1 月，我們完成了三筆關於聖塔安那盆地水抽水權的銷售交易，每英畝英呎的售價為 30,000 美元，總計 1.7 百萬美元，並記錄了 1.5 百萬美元的水權銷售獲利。
2025 年 3 月 1 日，我們收到了 PGIM 房地產金融 LLC ("PGIM") 發出的終止通知，關於 2023 年 1 月 31 日簽訂的農場管理協議 ("FMA")。FMA 於 2025 年 3 月 31 日終止。根據 FMA，我們為位於加州圖萊爾縣的 3,537 英畝土地（"北方財產"）提供農業、管理和運作服務，這些土地我們先前已出售給 PGIM。
於 2025 年 3 月 17 日，本公司宣佈本公司董事會批准了一項股票買回計畫，授權本公司買回最高 30.0 百萬美元的本公司流通普通股。此股票買回計畫可隨時修改、暫停或終止，且不表示本公司有義務買回任何股票。
於 2025 年 3 月 17 日，本公司宣佈本公司已完成探討潛在戰略選擇的程序，此程序係本公司於 2023 年 12 月 1 日先前公告。雖然此正式探討程序已結束，本公司仍致力於執行我們的綜合戰略路線圖，以創造長期股東價值。作為我們日常業務的一部分，我們將持續在評估潛在戰略合併與收購機會上保持靈活，同時也推進我們將非核心資產商業化的計畫。

於 2025 年 4 月 8 日，本公司宣佈本公司將與 Agromin Corporation 簽訂意向書，成立一間 50%/50% 的合資公司，Agromin Corporation 是加州最大的有機廢棄物回收公司，以大幅擴展 Agromin Corporation 成功的有機廢棄物回收計畫。該合資公司計畫將從現有的 15 英畝綠色廢棄物堆肥設施擴展至 70 英畝、商業規模的堆肥設施，處理綠色廢棄物與食物廢棄物。我們預期將進入該合資公司並開始建設，時間為財務年度 2026 年。
於 2025 年 4 月 9 日，本公司宣佈本公司收到一筆 10.0 百萬美元現金分紅，為本公司在實業合資公司 Harvest at Limoneira 中所佔的 20.0 百萬美元現金分紅，與 Lewis 羣公司（"Lewis"）共同持有。

於 2025 年 6 月 6 日，本公司與 Sunkist Growers, Inc. 簽訂商業包裝場許可協議，Sunkist Growers, Inc. 是一個非營利行銷合作組織（"Sunkist"），生效日期為 2025 年 11 月 1 日。此協議允許本公司對 Sunkist 種植者水果進行等級評定、標籤、包裝、準備行銷並運送，並在這些活動中使用 Sunkist 商標。此協議的初始期限為三年，並有自動一年延長條款。與我們決定將銷售與行銷業務合併至 Sunkist 的決定相關，我們在財務年度 2025 年第四季支出了約 0.7 百萬美元的現金與股票薪酬解僱費用。

於 2025 年 6 月 26 日，本公司與 AgWest Farm Credit, PCA（"Lender"）簽訂主貸款協議（"MLA"），日期為 2025 年 6 月 26 日，並附有循環信貸設施補充（"Revolving Credit Supplement"）及非循環信貸設施補充（"Non-Revolving Credit Supplement"，與循環信貸設施補充合稱為 "Supplements"）。此 MLA 修訂並取代我們與 Lender 之間的先前主貸款協議，並將本金償還期限延長至 2030 年 7 月 1 日。

headings: 與我們農業業務運作相關的風險
本公司決定自2025年11月1日起將柑橘銷售與行銷業務合併至Sunkist Growers, Inc.，此舉可能無法成功。
惡劣天氣條件、自然災害，包括地震與野火，以及其他自然條件，包括氣候變遷的影響，可能對本公司業務造成重大成本與損失。
本公司農業種植可能因疾病與害蟲而受損，這可能對本公司業務造成損失，且預防這些問題可能對本公司造成顯著額外成本。
本公司獲利對市場供給與價格以及產品需求的波動相當敏感。
本公司獲利可能受到季節性變動的影響。
農產品或原材料成本的增加，例如燃料與紙張，可能對本公司營運成果造成不利影響。
勞動力、人力與福利成本的增加可能對本公司營運成果造成不利影響。
移民法規的變更可能影響 Limoneira 收穫其農作物的能力。
缺乏足夠的水源將嚴重影響我們生產農作物或開發不動產的能力。
我們運營過程中使用除草劑、殺蟲劑及其他潛在危險物質，可能導致環境損害，並使我們產生更高的成本。
全球經濟衰退可能對我們產業的參與者產生不利影響，而此影響無法完全預測。
我們面臨產品污染及產品責任索償的風險。
我們面臨運輸風險。
與 LIMONEIRA 或我們其他商標及相關品牌或 Sunkist 有關的事件或流言，可能對我們業務產生重大影響。
政府規範可能提高我們的生產成本，並增加法律及規範費用。
我們依賴我們的基礎建設以確保有足夠的容量來處理我們每年的檸檬生產需求。
與我們負債相關的風險
我們可能無法產生足夠的現金流量以償還我們的債務義務。
我們的部分債務是以變動利率為基礎，若利率上升，可能會導致利息支出增加。
全球資本與信貸市場的問題會影響我們的流動性，提高我們的借款成本，並可能影響我們供應商與客戶的營運。
與我們不動產開發業務相關的風險
我們從事一個週期性產業，並受一般及地方經濟條件的變化影響。
全球經濟衰退，或國家或地區經濟情況下滑，可能會對我們的不動產開發業務產生不利影響。
較高的利率及缺乏資金來源可能對房地產業造成重大影響。
我們需面對各種土地使用規範，並需政府許可才能進行開發，這些許可有可能被拒絕。
第三方訴訟可能增加我們房地產開發工作的時間與成本。
我們需遵守環境規範，並可能面臨環保團體的反對，這可能會導致延宕並增加我們房地產開發工作的成本，甚至完全阻礙開發進行。
我們的房地產開發專案完全集中於加州。
若房地產業衰退，或房貸產業及商業房地產融資出現不穩定，可能會對我們的房地產業務產生負面影響。
我們依賴第三方顧問的契約安排來協助執行房地產開發專案，並面臨與這些安排相關的風險。
若我們無法在預期的時間與預算內完成土地開發專案，甚至無法完成，可能會對我們的財務結果產生負面影響。
若我們無法以合理成本或任何方式取得所需土地使用許可，將會對我們的營運成果造成不利影響。
若我們無法取得合理價格的融資以支持我們的不動產開發專案及土地開發活動，可能會導致淨收入減少或現金流減少。
我們可能面臨與Lewis Group of Companies所共同成立的不動產合資企業相關的風險，包括：
我們可能面臨其他風險，這些風險可能影響我們開發土地的能力。
一般風險及與我們普通股相關的風險
我們的業務具有高度競爭性，我們無法保證我們將維持目前的市場佔有率。
貨幣兌換波動可能影響我們營運的結果。
我們依賴關鍵人員，若失去其中一位或多位關鍵人員，可能會對我們的前景造成重大且不利的影響。
通貨膨脹可能對我們的營運產生重大不利影響。
取得其他企業可能對我們的營運收入造成風險。
我們的普通股價值可能波動。
我們普通股的集中持股會導致股價突然變動的風險。
我們的章程文件包含可能延宕、延後或防止控制權變更的條款。
我們因成為上市公司而產生更高的成本。
paragraphs: 本公司將柑橘銷售與行銷業務與 Sunkist 合併，使我們對銷售與行銷我們的檸檬業務的控制能力降低。 Sunkist 的行銷可能無效，這可能會導致柑橘銷售減少，特別是我們的檸檬銷售減少。 Sunkist 對柑橘銷售與行銷投入的資源不足，可能會減少我們的檸檬銷售，並對我們的營運與財務結果產生負面影響。
消費者與機構對 Sunkist 商標及相關品牌的認知，以及這些品牌與高品質與安全柑橘的關聯，是 Sunkist 商業的重要組成部分。任何導致消費者與/或機構不再將這些品牌與高品質與安全柑橘關聯的事件或流言，可能會對品牌價值與新鮮柑橘需求產生重大影響。
作為 Sunkist 授權的包裝廠，我們被要求從 Fruit Growers Supply Company（"FGS"），一家與 Sunkist 有關聯的製造與供應合作機構，購買大多數包裝材料。來自 FGS 的包裝材料成本增加或包裝材料運輸中斷，可能會對我們的營運收入產生負面影響。
Sunkist 的網路安全風險、資料保護違規、網路攻擊與系統整合問題，可能會干擾 Sunkist 的內部營運或對終端客戶提供的服務，而這種幹擾可能會減少我們預期的營收、增加我們的費用、損害我們的聲譽，並對我們的業務產生負面影響。
新鮮農產品易受不利天氣條件影響，包括風暴、洪水、乾旱與溫度極端，這些情況相當常見，且因氣候變遷的影響，未來可能發生頻率更高或預測性更低。不利的生長條件可能同時降低產量與品質。在極端情況下，某些地理區域的整季收成可能完全損失。我們為某些作物購買收成保險，這部分抵消我們的風險。
我們所有的作物都可能受到霜凍與結冰的損害，這在過去曾有週期性發生。在某些情況下，水果會受損或完全損壞；在持續寒冷的狀況下，樹木也可能受損或死亡。
